Read Oarfish Quantifications Into an IsoformicExperiment

Source: R/oarfish.R
read_oarfish.Rd

Oarfish quantifies long reads (Oxford Nanopore and PacBio) against a transcriptome. For every sample it writes, next to a common output prefix, <prefix>.quant (transcript name, length and estimated read count), <prefix>.ambig_info.tsv (reads that map to the transcript alone and reads shared with others), <prefix>.meta_info.json and, with --num-bootstraps, <prefix>.infreps.pq (the bootstrap replicates as a Parquet table). read_oarfish() reads them like read_salmon() reads Salmon output: an IsoformicExperiment with counts, length and abundance assays, and, with inferential = TRUE, the uncertainty tables of add_uncertainty().

Usage

read_oarfish(
  paths,
  annot_path,
  col_data = NULL,
  experiment_name = NULL,
  ignore_after_bar = TRUE,
  drop_unannotated = FALSE,
  inferential = FALSE
)

Arguments

paths

Output prefixes of Oarfish (the value of -o), paths to the .quant files, or directories holding a single .quant file. Names, when present, are the sample IDs; otherwise the prefix is used.

annot_path

Annotation directory or GFF3/GTF file (see prepare_isoformic_annotation()).

col_data

Optional data frame of sample metadata whose first column (or a sample_id column) matches the sample IDs. When NULL, a minimal table with just sample_id is created.

experiment_name

Optional experiment name.

ignore_after_bar

Logical. Keep only the part of transcript names before the first | (GENCODE FASTA headers used as Salmon references).

drop_unannotated

Logical. Drop transcripts absent from the annotation (with a message) instead of failing.

inferential

Logical. Read the bootstrap replicates and the ambiguity counts and compute the uncertainty tables with add_uncertainty(). The samples must have been quantified with --num-bootstraps.

Value

An IsoformicExperiment.

Details

Oarfish does not write TPM; the abundance assay is computed from the read counts and the transcript lengths (reads per base, scaled to one million). The ambiguity counts of .ambig_info.tsv play the role of the equivalence classes of Salmon in equivalence_support(): unique_fraction is the share of reads mapped to the transcript alone, while n_classes is not available. The functions read_inferential_replicates(), equivalence_support(), salmon_run_qc() and add_uncertainty() accept Oarfish prefixes as paths, but not together with Salmon directories.

Examples

prefixes <- file.path(
  system.file("extdata", "oarfish", package = "isoformic"),
  c("control_1", "control_2", "treated_1")
)
names(prefixes) <- basename(prefixes)
annot <- system.file(
  "extdata", "example_experiment", "annotation",
  package = "isoformic"
)
iso <- read_oarfish(prefixes, annot_path = annot, inferential = TRUE)
iso
#> <IsoformicExperiment> isoformic_4052008d1e
#>   annotation : gencode_v33_example_subset (69 genes, 892 transcripts, 7,032 exons)
#>   samples    : 3 [oarfish_num_processed, oarfish_num_mapped, oarfish_percent_mapped, oarfish_replicate_type, oarfish_num_replicates, oarfish_optimiser, oarfish_alignment_source, oarfish_prob_model, oarfish_qc_flag]
#>   transcripts: 72 assayed from 3 genes
#>   assays     : abundance, counts, length
#>   gene assays: derived from transcript assays on demand
#>   DE results : <none>
head(tx_uncertainty(iso))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 18
